audience: developers, founders and marketers evaluating an embeddable, deliberately powerless landing-page chat agent
objective: get them to try the interview and configurator on this page, then self-host from the GitHub repo
tone: clear, technically precise, honest about limits, no marketing fluff
docs:
Concierge is a deliberately powerless landing-page agent: an embeddable chat widget plus a small sandboxed proxy server. It answers visitor questions using ONLY a page's digested brief (a few hundred words of plain text the site owner wrote). It is open source (MIT) at github.com/yolo-maxi/concierge, built by repo.box, and it is live on frontier.repo.box and on concierge.repo.box itself.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It has no tools by default, no browser, no retrieval, no memory across sessions, no accounts, no booking or purchasing, and it cannot change its own configuration. If a question is not answered by the brief it says so and points to the call to action instead of guessing. It refuses off-topic requests, prompt injection, persona swaps and attempts to extract its instructions. Jailbreaking it yields at worst an off-brand sentence; there is nothing to escalate to.

HOW IT WORKS. The host page loads one script tag (or the React component). The widget holds no secrets, only an endpoint URL. It POSTs the transcript to the Concierge server's /chat endpoint. The server injects the page brief into a hardened system prompt, strips any client-supplied system role, caps message depth (24) and length (2000 chars), rate-limits per IP (default 20 per minute) and per session (12 per minute), bounds concurrency (4 active, 16 queued), times out cancelled work (30 s), opens a circuit after 3 provider failures, and streams the answer back as server-sent events. Each turn can be logged to Telegram or a webhook. The model is a small fast one (deepseek-v4-flash via Venice by default) through a typed provider adapter; Venice is the only supported provider today.

THE BRIEF. A brief is JSON with six required strings: brandName, audience, objective, tone, cta, docs. docs is the agent's entire world. Include a LINKS section listing the exact URLs it may share; it can only cite links that appear verbatim in the brief. One server can host one brief (CONCIERGE_BRIEF), a map of briefs selected by pageId (CONCIERGE_BRIEFS), or a versioned packet manifest (CONCIERGE_PACKET, manifestVersion 1, with defaultPageId and pages).

THEMING. The widget is token-first: 77 CSS custom properties named --cc-* control colours, radii, shadows, typography, spacing, layout and motion. Six presets ship: midnight (default), light, terminal, paper, neon, minimal. accentColor and accentColor2 derive the gradient; radiusScale and density (comfortable or compact) adjust shape; themeVars overrides any token. It mounts in a shadow root by default so host CSS cannot leak in and widget CSS cannot leak out; ::part(launcher) and ::part(panel) are exposed. Launcher styles: pill, bubble, bar, inline-input. Positions: bottom-right, bottom-left, or inline.

THE CONFIGURATOR ON THIS PAGE. concierge.repo.box has a guided interview that produces a valid brief, a live preview that answers from that brief through a short-lived server-side sandbox (30 minutes, powerless, rate-limited), a configurator for every token, and an export panel that emits the script tag, the brief JSON and a React snippet.

OPTIONAL CAPABILITY PACKS. Off by default and only configurable from server-side brief JSON, never from the browser: a retrieval pack (inline docs or a URL fetched once at boot, top-k chunks injected per turn) and an allowlist of server-defined tools such as capture_lead and handoff_human, plus an opt-in generative UI protocol (ui: true) that lets the model render declared components. Side-effect tools require confirmation and repeats are deduplicated. Client requests cannot enable any of these.

SELF-HOSTING. Clone the repo, pnpm install, copy server/.env.example to server/.env with a Venice API key and a brief path, pnpm dev:server for the proxy on port 8787, and build the widget with pnpm build. scripts/build-bundle.sh produces a single server bundle plus the embed file; scripts/deploy.sh has dry-run, staging, apply and rollback modes. GET /health reports liveness and queue/circuit state; GET /ready returns 503 when saturated. Error codes include queue_full, rate_limited_ip, rate_limited_session and provider_circuit_open. POST /brief/validate checks a brief without storing it.

PRICING. There is no hosted plan and nothing to pay repo.box for: it is MIT-licensed software you run yourself. Your only cost is the model provider.

WHO MADE IT. repo.box, an independent team building infrastructure for software that runs itself. They can be hired at repo.box/hire.
